A storm-lashed mountain peak, jagged crags falling away into churning cloud, lightning flickering on the horizon, the tower braced against howling wind, its stones slick with rain.
An enchanted misty forest stretching to a hazy horizon far below, ancient treetops catching the last gold light, fog pooling deep between their roots like still water.
A floating sky-island wreathed in cloud, other distant isles drifting lazily beyond, a great copper sun sinking behind them, painting the whole sky in amber and rose.
A rooftop terrace above a sprawling fantasy city, lamplit streets threading between towers and domes far below, smoke curling from a thousand chimneys into the violet dusk.
A moonlit moor rolling away in all directions, pale silver light on the heather, a distant standing stone just visible, the air cold and utterly still.
A rocky island rising from a vast grey sea, white surf battering the cliffs below, seabirds wheeling on the salt wind, a cold sun low and glittering on the water.
A deep autumn wood blazing with red and gold, the canopy far below like a smouldering fire, bare black branches threading through the colour, a thin mist in the hollows.
A snowy alpine valley cupped between white peaks, frozen lakes gleaming like mirrors far below, pines laden with snow, the air crystalline and sharp, the light a pale blue-white.
A cliff-edge above a great waterfall, the plunging water a white thunder below, mist rising in vast columns, a rainbow hanging faintly in the spray-filled afternoon air.
A wasteland under a strange bruised sky, cracked earth stretching in every direction, two sullen moons hanging low, the light a sickly green at the horizon, nothing moving.
A starlit night sky viewed from an open observatory platform, the Milky Way a river of cold fire overhead, planets glinting, the land below invisible and forgotten in the dark.
A green hill rolling away under a vast sunset, the sky layered in deep orange and crimson, a river catching the last light far below, rooks circling the valley's edge.
A coastal headland battered by a winter sea, iron-grey waves crashing far below, the horizon lost in driving rain, the tower's windows frosted with salt, a lighthouse winking distantly.
A sun-scorched desert plateau, red sand dunes rolling to every horizon under a bone-white sky, heat shimmer rising in columns, a dry riverbed tracing a pale line below.
A glacial ridge between two frozen peaks, blue ice falling away on both sides, crevasses splitting the glacier far below, the wind sharp enough to cut, the sky an empty pale.
A drowned valley turned to a vast inland lake, submerged ruins just visible in the clear shallows below, the water perfectly still, reflecting a grey overcast sky and the tower above it.
A volcanic caldera's rim, lava glowing deep orange in the crater below, toxic smoke drifting across a dark sky, the rocks underfoot warm, the air tasting of sulphur and ash.
A meadow valley in high summer, wildflowers carpeting the slopes below in white and yellow, a lazy river looping through it, bees audible even at this height, the light long and golden.
A jungle canopy stretching to every horizon, impossibly green under a grey monsoon sky, rain hammering the leaves far below, white mist rising between the trees like slow breath.
A tundra plain under the aurora borealis, flat frozen ground stretching endlessly below, the northern lights shifting green and violet overhead, the silence immense and pressing in on all sides.
A canyon system dropping away in sheer red walls below, a silver river threading through the distant floor, hawks riding thermals at eye level, the late sun striking the far cliff face orange.
A high alpine meadow in early spring, snow still on the peaks above and below, patches of bright new green appearing, streams of snowmelt catching the noon light like scattered glass.
A dark peat bog spreading below under a pewter sky, pools of black water gleaming between hummocks of brown grass, a distant carrion bird circling, the horizon flat and featureless.
A clifftop above a sea-cave labyrinth, turquoise water visible far below through the cave mouths, waves surging and retreating with a deep boom, the afternoon light flashing off the churning foam.
A hillside vineyard in late harvest, terraced rows dropping away below in deep burgundy and amber, the smell of pressed grapes carried upward, a low autumn sun warm and honeyed on the slopes.
